newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Shinhwa sees '97 sales at 200 bln won.
newsitem.headline: Shinhwa sees '97 sales at 200 bln won.

text.p: Shinhwa Co, a small telecommunications equipment producer, is targeting 1997 sales of 200 billion won, up sharply from 35 billion won in 1996, the company chairman told Reuters on Thursday.

Chairman Lee Eun-jo said in an interview the company's sales would reach one trillion won by 2000, thanks to sales of its newly developed communications and tracking devices for use by vehicles and small boats.
"Sales can grow even faster than that," Lee said.
He said Shinhwa, which had so far focused on production of leather goods, would begin marketing the Tacho Global Positioning System (TGPS) late this month.
The system, developed over the past three years, allows control centres to track and communicate with vehicles.

Lee said the system was a far more advanced device than the more widely known GPS system, which only tells information about vehicles' operations. He said the system was expected to help transportation companies save huge costs.
"The system, if fully supplied, would save about 30 percent of transportation costs for land cargo carriers," Lee said.
Land cargo transportation costs that South Korean companies pay annually are now estimated at 13 trillion won, he said.
South Korea is expected to have a network for use by TGPS devices by the end of March in the Seoul area and by the end of July elsewhere in the country.
